title: wt new --json
description: What a `wt new` run did, side effect by side effect. Printed by `wt new --json` as the only thing on stdout, also when a handled SIGINT or SIGTERM ends the run. Schema 1: fields may be added and enumerations may gain values; nothing is renamed or removed. See docs/json.md.

schema.description: The major version: a new one only for a change that breaks readers.

schemaVersion.description: The full semantic version of this schema that the output follows: minor for an added field or enumeration value, patch for wording.

outcome.description: created: the worktree made, every step done or skipped. createdWithProblems: the worktree made, and a step failed or was not run, or it is not on expectedCommit. refused: nothing made, see problems. failed: git worktree add failed and left no worktree. interrupted: a signal ended the run.

error.description: Why it was refused, or stopped before planning (not in a git repository).

problems.description: Why it was refused, or what is wrong with the worktree made that no step names. As in the plan, plus planChanged and headMoved.

base.description: For wt new: what the branch was cut from: as given with --base, else trunk, or origin/<trunk> when local trunk was behind it (since 1.3.0). Null for wt checkout.

expectedCommit.description: The commit the plan pinned: the base's for wt new, the branch's for wt checkout.

commit.description: The new worktree's HEAD, read after it was created; null when none was.

steps.description: Every side effect, always all eight, in this order: worktree, branch, config, cache (since 1.1.0 for wt new, 1.2.0 for wt checkout; before, seven steps), provision, submodules, build, superset. A step that was skipped or not reached still has its row.

baseSource.description: Null when the run stopped before it planned. Where base comes from (since 1.3.0): local — the local trunk branch, which is equal to origin/<trunk>, ahead of it, diverged from it, or has no origin/<trunk> to compare with; remote — origin/<trunk>, because local trunk is behind it; base — what --base named. wt new fetches trunk first unless --no-fetch or --base is given, and --dry-run does too, so this is as of that fetch (a failed fetch leaves origin/<trunk> as last fetched).

app.description: The app's name, as `devports config --json` reports it.

url.description: `https://<name>.<domain>`: where the app is reached when its dev server runs, with the name devports gives the worktree and the app's `domain:`.

addresses.description: Since 1.2.0: where the new worktree's dev servers are reached, one {app, url} per app that devports config --json gives a domain, in the order it lists them, the url being https://<name>.<domain> with the name devports gives the worktree. Always present: empty when no app has a domain, or devports is not installed, fails, does not answer within two seconds, or is too old to report domains (wt does not read .dev-ports.yaml itself). Nothing is routed by wt: the address works once the dev server runs.

code.description: The plan's problems, and planChanged (--expect no longer holds), headMoved (the worktree is not on expectedCommit).

result.description: worktree: created (with a reason when git failed after making it), failed. branch: created (wt new), untouched (wt checkout). config, cache, provision, submodules, build: done, skipped, failed; cache is done with a reason naming any cache the filesystem could not clone. superset: registered, skipped, failed. Any step: notRun, interrupted.

commit.description: worktree: its HEAD. branch: its tip.

reason.description: Why, for skipped, failed and interrupted; a note otherwise.
